Note that we can rewrite this integral as

$$
{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{20}{25-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{4}{5}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{1-{(\frac{x}{5})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for the inverse hyperbolic tangent,

$$
\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{artanh}⁡u+C,
$$

the only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have ${(\frac{x}{5})}^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{x}{5}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{5}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=5\,\text{d}u.
$$

Before substituting, we use the table below to change the limits from $x$ to $u.$

| $x$ | $0$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\frac{3}{5}$ |

Using the above, we can now write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{20}{25-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{4}{5}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{1-{(\frac{x}{5})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{5}{\int }_{0}^{3/5}\frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\cdot 5\,\text{d}u \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{3/5}\frac{\text{d}u}{1-{u}^{2}} \\  & =4\operatorname{artanh}⁡u\,{|}_{0}^{3/5} \\  & =4\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\frac{3}{5})-4\operatorname{artanh}⁡0 \\  & =4\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\frac{3}{5})\end{aligned}
$$
